newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen listings up 22 pct in Jan-May period.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen listings up 22 pct in Jan-May period.

text.p: The Shenzhen Stock Exchange received 59 new listings in the first five months of 1997, a 22 percent increase from the end of 1996, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said on Tuesday.
The new listings represent a total of 2.6 billion shares, statistics from the Shenzhen bourse showed.
At the end of 1996, the Shenzhen stock market had 270 listed stocks, including 227 domestic currency A counters and 43 foreign currency B issues, it said.
The newcomers, mostly large- and medium-scale state enterprises, raised combined proceeds of more than 16 billion yuan, the newspaper said.
The new issues have an average per-share earnings of 0.512 yuan in 1996, it said.

Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Ltd topped the 59 listings with 1996 earnings per share of 1.3 yuan, while Hainan Dadonghai Tourism Centre (Holdings) Co Ltd posted the weakest per-share earnings of 0.185 yuan, it said.
About half the newcomers are based in the centre or west of China, in line with Beijing's policy of narrowing the gap between the richer coastal provinces and the poorer western areas, it said.
